newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales light at $64-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales light at $64-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday Thursday was light at $64.00 per cwt, steady with active sales on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 head sold in Kansas, which brought the week to date movement near 89,000 head. There were no reported sales in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.
Most of the Panhandle showlist reportedly was sold out following week to date movement near 130,000 head.
Several Kansas feedlot managers reported having some cattle left to sell and were pricing them at $65.00 against packer bids at $64.00.
Most of this week's cattle sales took place after midday on Wednesday at $64.00, unchanged from last week.
Fed cattle prices were bolstered by a decline in market-ready cattle supplies this week and recent strength in boxed beef prices, the feedlot sources said.
However, fed cattle prices were unable to reach $65.00 amid ideas that beef prices were near a top and ready to trend lower, they said.
Heavyweight choice beef Wednesday was quoted at $102.81 per cwt, down $0.28 from Tuesday, after advancing $4.05 since July 10, USDA statistics showed.
